    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)
  • Reconnect the APIM connector. Make sure it seats and latches correctly.
  • Wait at least 2 minutes for the APIM to re-initialize.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable TSBs. If a TSB exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW TSB instructions. If no TSBs address this concern, INSTALL a new APIM. Refer to the appropriate Removal and Installation procedure in Section 415-00.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.



Pinpoint Test V: The RH Steering Wheel Controls Are Inoperative Or Do Not Operate Correctly

Diagnostic Overview

Diagnostics in this manual assume a certain skill level and knowledge of Ford-specific diagnostic practices. Refer to Diagnostic Methods in Section  100-00 for information about these practices.


Refer to Wiring Diagrams Cell 130 , Audio System/Navigation for schematic and connector information.

Normal Operation and Fault Conditions

Refer to Steering Wheel Switch Functions and Steering Wheel Switches in Information and Entertainment System.



  DTC Fault Trigger Conditions


DTC Description Fault Trigger Conditions
B1380:09 Steering Wheel Right Switch Pack: Component Failure Set by the SCCM when the RH steering wheel switch is stuck.
B1380:11 Steering Wheel Right Switch Pack: Circuit Short To Ground Set by the SCCM when a short to ground is detected in the RH steering wheel switch circuits.
B1380:17 Steering Wheel Right Switch Pack: Circuit Voltage Above Threshold Set by the SCCM when a short to voltage is detected in the RH steering wheel switch circuits.


Possible Sources

  • Wiring, terminals, or connectors
  • Clockspring
  • Steering wheel switch
  • SCCM
PINPOINT TEST V : THE RH STEERING WHEEL CONTROLS ARE INOPERATIVE OR DO NOT OPERATE CORRECTLY
V1  CHECK THE RH STEERING WHEEL SWITCH PIDS
  • Ignition ON.
  • Monitor the steering wheel controls PIDs while pressing each RH steering wheel switch.
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, view the SCCM PIDs.

    PID Group One

    • SW_VOLDOWN
    • SW_VOLUP
    • SW_SEEKMINUS
    • SW_SEEKPLUS
    • SW_MEDIA

    PID Group Two

    • SW_VOICE
    • SW_PHONE

Do the PID values agree with the switch positions?

Yes GO to V10.
No PID Group One: If one or more but not all of thesePIDs (SW_VOLDOWN, SW_VOLUP, SW_SEEKMINUS, SW_SEEKPLUS, and SW_MEDIA) are incorrect or always read one particular switch position, INSTALL a new RH steering wheel switch. REFER to Section  211-05.
PID Group Two: If either the SW_VOICE or SW_PHONE PIDs is incorrect or always read one particular switch position, INSTALL a new RH steering wheel switch. REFER to Section  211-05.
For all other concerns, GO to V2.


V2  CHECK FOR IPC DTC U0212:00
  • Ignition ON.
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, clear the DTCs from the IPC .
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Ignition ON.
  • Wait at least 10 seconds.
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the IPC self-test.

Is DTC U0212:00 set in the IPC ?

Yes REFER to Section  413-01.
No GO to V3.


V3  CHECK THE CIRCUITRY BETWEEN THE CLOCKSPRING AND STEERING WHEEL CONTROLS FOR A SHORT TO GROUND

WARNING: Turn the ignition OFF and wait one minute to deplete the backup power supply. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious personal injury or death in the event of an accidental deployment.

  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect: RH Steering Wheel Switch C2999.
  • Disconnect: Clockspring C218B.
  • Measure the resistance between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2999 Pin 2   VME14 — Ground
    C2999 Pin 4   RME14 — Ground
    C2999 Pin 6   VME54 — Ground
    C2999 Pin 7   RME54 — Ground



Are the resistances greater than 10,000 ohms?

Yes GO to V4.
No INSTALL a new steering wheel. REFER to Section  211-04.


V4  CHECK THE CIRCUITRY BETWEEN THE CLOCKSPRING AND STEERING WHEEL CONTROLS FOR AN OPEN
  • Measure the resistance between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2999 Pin 2   VME14 C218B Pin 14   VME14
    C2999 Pin 4   RME14 C218B Pin 6   RME14
    C2999 Pin 6   VME54 C218B Pin 16   VME54
    C2999 Pin 7   RME54 C218B Pin 8   RME54



Are the resistances less than 3 ohms?

Yes GO to V5.
No INSTALL a new steering wheel. REFER to Section  211-04.


V5  CHECK THE CIRCUITRY BETWEEN THE CLOCKSPRING AND STEERING WHEEL CONTROLS FOR A SHORT TOGETHER
  • Measure the resistance between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2999 Pin 2   VME14 C2999 Pin 4   RME14
    C2999 Pin 6   VME54 C2999 Pin 7   RME54



Are the resistances greater than 10,000 ohms?

Yes GO to V6.
No INSTALL a new steering wheel. REFER to Section  211-04.


V6  CHECK THE CLOCKSPRING FOR A SHORT TO GROUND
  • Connect: Clockspring C218B.
  • Disconnect: Clockspring C218C.
  • Measure the resistance between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2999 Pin 2   VME14 — Ground
    C2999 Pin 4   RME14 — Ground
    C2999 Pin 6   VME54 — Ground
    C2999 Pin 7   RME54 — Ground



Are the resistances greater than 10,000 ohms?

Yes GO to V7.
No INSTALL a new clockspring. REFER to Section  501-20B.


V7  CHECK THE CLOCKSPRING FOR AN OPEN
  • Measure the resistance between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2999 Pin 2   VME14 C218C Pin 6   —
    C2999 Pin 4   RME14 C218C Pin 5   —
    C2999 Pin 6   VME54 C218C Pin 10   —
    C2999 Pin 7   RME54 C218C Pin 9   —



Are the resistances less than 3 ohms?

Yes GO to V8.
No INSTALL a new clockspring. REFER to Section  501-20B.


V8  CHECK THE CLOCKSPRING FOR A SHORT TOGETHER
  • Measure the resistance between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2999 Pin 2   VME14 C2999 Pin 4   RME14
    C2999 Pin 6   VME54 C2999 Pin 7   RME54



Are the resistances greater than 10,000 ohms?

Yes GO to V9.
No INSTALL a new clockspring. REFER to Section  501-20B.


V9  CHECK FOR VOLTAGE AT THE SCCM
  • Ignition ON.
  • Measure the voltage between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2414D Pin 6   — C2414D Pin 5   —
    C2414D Pin 10   — C2414D Pin 9   —



Is approximately 5 volts present?

Yes INSTALL a new RH steering wheel switch. REFER to Section  211-05.
No GO to V10.


V10  CHECK FOR CORRECT SCCM OPERATION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect and inspect all the SCCM connectors.
  • Repair:
    • Corrosion (clean module pins or install new connectors or terminals)
    • Damaged or bent pins (install new terminals or pins)
    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)
  • Reconnect the SCCM connectors. Make sure they seat and latch correctly.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable TSBs. If a TSB exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW TSB instructions. If no TSBs address this concern, INSTALL a new SCCM . REFER to Section  211-05.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.



Pinpoint Test W: The Audio System Does Not Operate Correctly From The FCIM

Diagnostic Overview

Diagnostics in this manual assume a certain skill level and knowledge of Ford-specific diagnostic practices. Refer to Diagnostic Methods in Section  100-00 for information about these practices.

Normal Operation and Fault Conditions

Refer to Accessory Delay Feature, Audio Extended Play, and FCIM in Information and Entertainment System.

Possible Sources

  • Network communication concern
  • FCIM
PINPOINT TEST W : THE AUDIO SYSTEM DOES NOT OPERATE CORRECTLY FROM THE FCIM
W1  CHECK THE FDIM OPERATION
  • Verify the FDIM screen operation.

Does the FDIM operate correctly?

Yes GO to W2.
No GO to Pinpoint Test XA.


W2  VERIFY THAT THE ACM , APIM , AND FCIM PASS THE NETWORK TEST
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the network test.

Did the ACM , APIM , and FCIM pass the network test?

Yes GO to W3.
No If the ACM failed the network test, REFER to Section  418-00 The ACM Does Not Respond To The Scan Tool.
If the APIM failed the network test, REFER to Section  418-00 The APIM Does Not Respond To The Scan Tool.
If the FCIM failed the network test, REFER to Section  418-00 The FCIM Does Not Respond To The Scan Tool.


W3  RESET THE AUDIO SYSTEM MODULES AND RECHECK THE FCIM OPERATION
  • Disconnect the battery for 5 minutes, then reconnect it.
  • Turn the infotainment system on.
  • Test the FCIM for normal operation.

Does the FCIM operate correctly?

Yes The FCIM is operating correctly at this time. The concern was corrected by resetting the audio system modules.
No GO to W4.


W4  RETRIEVE THE ACM , APIM , AND FCIM DTCS
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the self-test for the following modules:
    • ACM
    • APIM
    • FCIM

Are any DTCs present in the ACM , APIM , or FCIM ?

Yes For ACM DTCs, REFER to the ACM DTC Chart in Information and Entertainment System
For APIM DTCs, REFER to the APIM DTC Chart in Information and Entertainment System
For FCIM DTCs, REFER to the FCIM DTC Chart in Information and Entertainment System
No GO to W5.


W5  CHECK FOR CORRECT FCIM OPERATION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect and inspect the FCIM connector.
  • Repair:
    • Corrosion (clean module pins or install new connectors or terminals)
    • Damaged or bent pins (install new terminals or pins)
    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)
  • Reconnect the FCIM connector. Make sure it seats and latches correctly.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable TSBs. If a TSB exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW TSB instructions. If no TSBs address this concern, INSTALL a new FCIM . REFER to Front Controls Interface Module (FCIM).
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.



Pinpoint Test XA: The FDIM Is Inoperative Or Does Not Operate Correctly

Diagnostic Overview

Normal Operation and Fault Conditions

Information and Entertainment System.



  DTC Fault Trigger Conditions


DTC Description Fault Trigger Conditions
B108E:01 Display: General Electrical Failure Sets in the APIM when an error is detected from the FDIM .
U0162:00 Lost Communication With Navigation Display Module: No Sub Type Information Set by the APIM when an internal connection concern or internal LCD panel concern is detected in the FDIM .


Possible Sources

  • Communication network concern
  • Uncalibrated touchscreen
  • Configuration concern
  • Object pressed against the FDIM
  • FDIM
  • APIM
PINPOINT TEST XA : THE FDIM IS INOPERATIVE OR DOES NOT OPERATE CORRECTLY
XA1  REBOOT THE APIM AND RECHECK THE SYSTEM OPERATION
  • Ignition ON.
  • Simultaneously press and hold the SEEK UP and POWER buttons on the FCIM for 10 seconds. As the APIM reboot begins, the touchscreen turns black before the startup sequence begins.
  • After the reboot is complete, operate the system to verify if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes If the FDIM is blank or black, GO to XA4.
If the image shown on the FDIM is incorrect, the image color is incorrect, or the image is distorted, flickering, or unclear, GO to XA12.
If the FDIM is frozen, GO to XA2.
If the FDIM is unresponsive to touch, GO to XA2.
If the FDIM is slow to respond, GO to XA10.
For all other concerns, GO to XA4.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. VERIFY the customer specific concern by duplicating the steps that were taken when the original concern was generated.


XA2  CHECK FOR THE AUDIO SYSTEM VOLUME POP-UP ON THE FDIM WHILE ADJUSTING THE AUDIO SYSTEM VOLUME
  • Operate the audio system in AM/FM mode.
  • Observe the FDIM while adjusting the audio system volume up and down.

Does the FDIM display the audio system volume pop-up when the volume is adjusted up and down?

Yes If the volume pop-up is displayed and the audio system output volume responds, GO to XA10.
If the volume pop-up is displayed but no sound is heard, REFER to the Symptom Charts in this section to diagnose the inoperative audio system feature(s).
No GO to XA3.


XA3  ENSURE THE TOUCHSCREEN IS CALIBRATED
  • Calibrate the touchscreen. Refer to Touchscreen Calibration.
  • Verify the touchscreen operation.

Does the FDIM touchscreen respond correctly?

Yes The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern was a result of the touchscreen not being calibrated.
No GO to XA13.


XA4  VERIFY THAT THE MODULES PASS THE NETWORK TEST
  • NOTE: A concern with the CAN may cause the FDIM touchscreen to be blank.

    Using the diagnostic scan tool, perform the network test.

Do all modules pass the network test?

Yes GO to XA5.
No Refer to Section  418-00.


XA5  VERIFY THE APIM IGNITION STATE PID
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, view the APIM PIDs .
  • Monitor the Ignition State PID (KEYPOS).
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Ignition ON.

Does the PID value match the actual switch positions?

Yes GO to XA6.
No DIAGNOSE the ignition switch input. Refer to Section  211-05.


XA6  CHECK FOR DTC U0162:00 SET IN THE APIM
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the APIM self-test.

Is DTC U0162:00 set in the APIM ?

Yes GO to XA7.
No GO to XA8.


XA7  CLEAR THE APIM DIAGNOSTIC TROUBLE CODES (DTCS) AND RECHECK FOR DTC U0162:00
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, clear the APIM Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) and repeat the APIM self-test.

Is DTC U0162:00 still set in the APIM ?

Yes GO to XA14.
No GO to XA8.


XA8  CHECK FOR DTC B108E:01 SET IN THE APIM
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the APIM self-test.

Is DTC B108E:01 set in the APIM ?

Yes GO to XA9.
No GO to XA13.


XA9  CLEAR THE APIM DIAGNOSTIC TROUBLE CODES (DTCS) AND RECHECK FOR DTC B108E:01
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, clear the APIM DTCs and repeat the APIM self-test.

Is DTC B108E:01 set in the APIM ?

Yes GO to XA13.
No GO to XA14.


XA10  INSPECT THE DISPLAY FOR CRACKS
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Remove the FCIM . REFER to Front Controls Interface Module (FCIM).
  • NOTE: Minor cracks on the display can cause touch concerns.

    Carefully inspect the FDIM screen for cracks. The RGB Pixel Test and Display Test Pattern functions available through APIM Bezel Diagnostics can be used to assist in the inspection. REFER to Bezel Diagnostics.

Are any cracks present on the FDIM display?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable service articles: TSB , General Service Bulletin (GSB), SSM or FSA . If a service article exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW the service article instructions. If no service articles address this concern, INSTALL a new FDIM. Refer to the appropriate Removal and Installation procedure in Section 415-00.
No GO to XA11.


XA11  CONFIRM THE FDIM TOUCH RESPONSE WITH THE FCIM REMOVED

NOTE: The FDIM can only sense one touch command at a time. If any objects are pressed against the touchscreen (including wiring or components behind the trim panel surrounding the FDIM ), the FDIM can appear to be inoperative.

  • Connect the FCIM electrical connectors, but do not install it.
  • Ignition ON.
  • Access the Bezel Diagnostics. Refer to Bezel Diagnostics.
  • NOTE: The touchscreen is a resistive touch panel. This means that a finer touch point result in a more responsive touch panel. For example, the tip of a finger nail result in better response than the broad surface of the thumb.

    After initiating the Touchscreen Activation Test, touch several points around the display and observe the display touch response. The most recent touch point is indicated by a blue box and prior touch points are indicated by white boxes.

Does the FDIM respond correctly to each touch point?

Yes If the FDIM responds correctly, the system is operating correctly at this time. REINSTALL the FCIM and ensure the FCIM opening is properly aligned with the FDIM and that no objects are in contact with the FDIM touchscreen. VERIFY the customer specific concern by duplicating the steps that were taken when the original concern was generated.
No GO to XA14.


XA12  INSPECT THE FDIM IMAGE CLARITY
  • Access Bezel Diagnostics. Refer to Bezel Diagnostics.
  • While using the RGB Pixel Test and Display Test Pattern functions, inspect the display image quality.

Is the image quality concern present when using the RGB Pixel Test and Display Test Pattern functions?

Yes GO to XA13.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. VERIFY the customer specific concern by duplicating the steps that were taken when the original concern was generated.


XA13  CHECK THE FDIM TO APIM CONNECTION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Remove the FDIM and separate the FDIM and APIM . REFER to Front Display Interface Module (FDIM).
  • NOTICE: Be careful not to damage the APIM and FDIM when inspecting and cleaning the connection.

    Inspect and clean the connection between the FDIM and APIM using compressed air.
  • Install the FDIM and APIM . Make sure the APIM is properly fastened to the FDIM and all connectors seat and latch correctly.
  • Ignition ON.
  • TEST the system for normal operation.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable service articles: TSB , General Service Bulletin (GSB), SSM or FSA . If a service article exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW the service article instructions. If no service articles address this concern, INSTALL a new FDIM. Refer to the appropriate Removal and Installation procedure in Section 415-00. If the concern is still present after FDIM replacement, GO to XA14.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The DTC may have been set due to an intermittent fault in the connection between the FDIM and APIM .


XA14  CHECK FOR CORRECT APIM OPERATION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect and inspect the APIM connector.
  • Repair:
    • Corrosion (clean module pins or install new connectors or terminals)
    • Damaged or bent pins (install new terminals or pins)
    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)
  • Reconnect the APIM connector. Make sure it seats and latches correctly.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable service articles: TSB , General Service Bulletin (GSB), SSM or FSA . If a service article exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW the service article instructions. If no service articles address this concern, INSTALL a new APIM. Refer to the appropriate Removal and Installation procedure in Section 415-00.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.



Pinpoint Test Y: Navigation Application Is Inoperative Or Unresponsive (If Equipped)

Diagnostic Overview

Diagnostics in this manual assume a certain skill level and knowledge of Ford-specific diagnostic practices. Refer to Diagnostic Methods in Section  100-00 for information about these practices.

Normal Operation and Fault Conditions

Refer to Navigation in Information and Entertainment System.

Removal of the navigation map data secure digital (SD) card results in the loss of navigation while the card is removed. This is normal operation.



  DTC Fault Trigger Conditions


DTC Description Fault Trigger Conditions
B1215:00 External Memory Card: No Sub Type Information Set by the APIM when the navigation map data secure digital (SD) card is missing.


Possible Sources

  • Media hub
  • Navigation map secure digital (SD) card not present, not fully seated, or damaged
  • Communications network concern
  • GPSM
  • APIM
PINPOINT TEST Y : NAVIGATION APPLICATION IS INOPERATIVE OR UNRESPONSIVE (IF EQUIPPED)
Y1  DETERMINE IF THE VEHICLE IS EQUIPPED WITH A FACTORY-INSTALLED NAVIGATION SYSTEM
  • Ensure that the correct VIN was entered on the technician service publication website.
  • Hover the mouse cursor over or click on the OASIS tab toward the top LH corner of the screen.
  • Select "HVBoM (Historical Vehicle Bill of Material)"
  • Locate the Limit to Base: text entry box toward the center of the screen.
  • Enter the navigation data secure digital (SD) card base part number "19H449" (do not include quotation marks).
  • Press Enter on the keyboard or click on "View BoM (Build of Material)".
    • If the vehicle is equipped with a factory-installed navigation system, a row will appear indicating "CARD - MEMORY" in the DESCRIPTION column.
    • If the vehicle is not equipped with a factory-installed navigation system, a row will not appear and the DESCRIPTION column will be blank.

Does the technician service publication website indicate the vehicle is equipped with a factory-installed navigation system?

Yes GO to Y2.
No Ford Motor Company does not support the addition of a navigation system to vehicles not equipped with a factory-installed navigation system.


Y2  VERIFY THE APIM PASSES THE NETWORK TEST
  • Using the diagnostic scan tool, perform the network test.

Did the APIM pass the network test?

Yes GO to Y3.
No REFER to Section  418-00. See The APIM Does Not Respond to the Diagnostic Scan Tool.


Y3  CHECK THE USB PORTS FOR POWER OUTPUT
  • Connect Multi-Media Interface Tester 105-00120.

Does the Multi-Media Interface Tester 105-00120 power on from both USB ports?

Yes GO to Y4.
No If the Multi-Media Interface Tester 105-00120 powers on from only one USB port, INSTALL a new media hub. REFER to Media Hub.
If the Multi-Media Interface Tester 105-00120 does not power on from either USB port, GO to Pinpoint Test Q.


Y4  RESET THE APIM AND VERIFY OPERATION OF THE USB CABLE
  • Remove any devices connected to the media hub.
  • Carry out an APIM power reset by disconnecting the battery for 1 minute, then reconnecting it.
  • Wait at least 2 minutes for the APIM to re-initialize.
  • Connect Multi-Media Interface Tester 105-00120.
  • Using the Multi-Media Interface Tester 105-00120, attempt to play an audio file using each USB port.

Is the audio output OK for each USB port?

Yes GO to Y5.
No If the audio output is not OK from one USB port, INSTALL a new media hub. REFER to Media Hub.
If the audio output is not OK from from both USB ports, GO to Pinpoint Test R.


Y5  CHECK FOR A NAVIGATION MAP DATA SECURE DIGITAL (SD) CARD FAULT MESSAGE
  • Ignition ON.
  • Observe the FDIM display.

Does the FDIM display "SD CARD FAULT?"

Yes GO to Y6.
No GO to Y9.


Y6  VERIFY THE NAVIGATION MAP DATA SECURE DIGITAL (SD) CARD IS PRESENT
  • Check for the presence of a navigation map data secure digital (SD) card in the media hub secure digital (SD) card slot.

Is the navigation map secure digital (SD) card present and fully seated?

Yes GO to Y7.
No If a non-Ford supplied secure digital (SD) card is present, EXPLAIN to the customer that only a Ford supplied map data card will work with the navigation system. INSTALL the navigation map secure digital (SD) card. TEST the system for normal operation.


Y7  INSPECT THE NAVIGATION MAP SECURE DIGITAL (SD) CARD

NOTE: The media hub secure digital (SD) card slot is spring loaded. To remove the secure digital (SD) card, push the card inward and release it. Do not attempt to forcefully pull the secure digital (SD) card from the secure digital (SD) card slot. This may cause damage to the secure digital (SD) card pins.

  • Remove the navigation map data secure digital (SD) card.
  • Inspect the navigation map data secure digital (SD) card case and pins for damage.

Is any damage present?

Yes INSTALL a new navigation map data secure digital (SD) card.
No If a known good map data secure digital (SD) card is available, GO to Y8.
If a known good map data secure digital (SD) card is NOT available, GO to Y9.


Y8  VERIFY NAVIGATION SYSTEM OPERATION WITH KNOWN GOOD MAP DATA SECURE DIGITAL (SD) CARD
  • Insert a known good navigation map data secure digital (SD) card with the correct software version level.
  • Confirm the navigation system operates correctly.

Does the navigation system operate correctly with the known good navigation map data secure digital (SD) card?

Yes INSTALL a new navigation map data secure digital (SD) card.
No GO to Y9.


Y9  CHECK FOR DIAGNOSTIC SCAN TOOL COMMUNICATION WITH THE GPSM
  • Ignition ON.
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the network test.

Does the diagnostic scan tool communicate with the GPSM ?

Yes GO to Y10.
No REFER to Section  418-00 The GPSM Does Not Respond To The Scan Tool.


Y10  RETRIEVE THE DTCS FROM THE APIM AND GPSM
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the self-test for the following modules:
    • APIM
    • GPSM

Are any DTCs present in the APIM or GPSM ?

Yes For APIM DTCs, REFER to the APIM DTC Chart in Information and Entertainment System
For GPSM DTCs, REFER to the GPSM DTC Chart in Information and Entertainment System
No GO to Y11.


Y11  REPROGRAM THE APIM
  • Perform the APIM Standard Programming. REFER to Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) Standard Programming
  • Override the Service Pack installation and perform a Full Flash/Force CIP .
  • Once the APIM programming is complete and the system has re-initialized, confirm the navigation system operates correctly.

Does the navigation system operate correctly?

Yes The navigation system is operating correctly at this time. The concern was resolved by reprogramming the APIM .
No GO to Y12.


Y12  CHECK FOR CORRECT GPSM OPERATION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect and inspect the GPSM connector.
  • Repair:
    • Corrosion (clean module pins or install new connectors or terminals)
    • Damaged or bent pins (install new terminals or pins)
    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)
  • Reconnect the GPSM connector. Make sure it seats and latches correctly.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable TSBs. If a TSB exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW TSB instructions. If no TSBs address this concern, INSTALL a new GPSM . REFER to Global Positioning System Module (GPSM).
If the concern is still present, GO to Y13.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.


Y13  CHECK FOR CORRECT APIM OPERATION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect and inspect the APIM connector.
  • Repair:
    • Corrosion (clean module pins or install new connectors or terminals)
    • Damaged or bent pins (install new terminals or pins)
    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)
  • Reconnect the APIM connector. Make sure it seats and latches correctly.
  • Wait at least 2 minutes for the APIM to re-initialize.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable TSBs. If a TSB exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW TSB instructions. If no TSBs address this concern, INSTALL a new APIM. Refer to the appropriate Removal and Installation procedure in Section 415-00.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.

Did the APIM and GPSM pass the network test?

Yes GO to Z2.
No If the APIM failed the network test, REFER to Section  418-00 The APIM Does Not Respond To The Scan Tool.
If the GPSM failed the network test, REFER to Section  418-00 The GPSM Does Not Respond To The Scan Tool.


Z2  RETRIEVE THE APIM AND GPSM DTCS
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the self-test for the following modules:
    • APIM
    • GPSM

Are any DTCs present in the APIM or GPSM ?

Yes For APIM DTCs, REFER to the APIM DTC Chart in Information and Entertainment System
For GPSM DTCs, REFER to the GPSM DTC Chart in Information and Entertainment System
No GO to Z3.


Z3  CHECK FOR CORRECT GPSM OPERATION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect and inspect the GPSM connector.
  • Repair:
    • Corrosion (clean module pins or install new connectors or terminals)
    • Damaged or bent pins (install new terminals or pins)
    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)
  • Reconnect the GPSM connector. Make sure it seats and latches correctly.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable TSBs. If a TSBTSB exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW TSBTSB instructions. If no TSBs address this concern, INSTALL a new GPSM . REFER to Global Positioning System Module (GPSM).
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.

Diagnostic Overview

Diagnostics in this manual assume a certain skill level and knowledge of Ford-specific diagnostic practices. Refer to Diagnostic Methods in Section  100-00 for information about these practices.



  DTC Fault Trigger Conditions


DTC Description Fault Trigger Conditions
U0100:00 Lost Communication with ECM/PCM "A": No Sub Type Information Set by the GPSM when network messages are missing from the PCM for more than 5 seconds with the ignition in RUN.

AA1  VERIFY THE CUSTOMER'S CONCERN

    Ignition ON.

Yes GO to AA2.

Yes GO to AA3.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The DTC may have been set due to high network traffic or an intermittent fault condition.

For DTC U3003:17, GO to Pinpoint Test AK.

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable TSBs. If a TSB exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW TSB instructions. If no TSBs address this concern, INSTALL a new PCM . REFER to Section  303-14.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.

Yes GO to AG3.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The DTC may have been set due to high network traffic or an intermittent fault condition.


AG3  CHECK FOR BATTERY VOLTAGE OUT-OF-RANGE DTCS
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the self-test for the following modules:
    • ACM
    • APIM

Are low or high voltage DTCs recorded in the ACM or APIM ?

Yes For DTC U3003:16, GO to Pinpoint Test AJ.
For DTC U3003:17, GO to Pinpoint Test AK.
No GO to AG4.

  • Ignition OFF.

    • Corrosion (clean module pins or install new connectors or terminals)

    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)

  • Wait at least 2 minutes for the APIM to re-initialize.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes CHECK OASIS for any applicable TSBs. If a TSB exists for this concern, DISCONTINUE this test and FOLLOW TSB instructions. If no TSBs address this concern, INSTALL a new APIM. Refer to the appropriate Removal and Installation procedure in Section 415-00.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. The concern may have been caused by module connections. ADDRESS the root cause of any connector or pin issues.

  • For the ACM , measure the voltage between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C240A Pin 1   SBP29 (GY/RD) — Ground


  • For the APIM , measure the voltage between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2383 Pin 1   SBP02 (YE/RD) — Ground


  • For the FCIM , measure the voltage between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2402 Pin 1   SBP09 (RD) — Ground


  • For the GPSM , measure the voltage between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2398 Pin 1   SBP09 (RD) — Ground



Is the voltage within 0.2 volts of the recorded battery voltage?

Yes GO to AJ5.
No REPAIR the circuit for high resistance.


AJ5  CHECK THE SUSPECT MODULE GROUND CIRCUIT FOR CONTINUITY

    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C240A Pin 1   SBP29 (GY/RD) C240A Pin 13   GD114 (BK/BU)

    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit

    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2402 Pin 1   SBP09 (RD) C2402 Pin 4   GD133 (BK)


  • For the GPSM , measure the voltage between:


    Positive Lead Negative Lead
    Pin Circuit Pin Circuit
    C2398 Pin 1   SBP09 (RD) C2398 Pin 6   GD114 (BK/BU)



Is the suspect module voltage greater than 11 volts?

Yes For the ACM , GO to AJ6.
For the APIM , GO to AJ7.
For the FCIM , GO to AJ8.
For the GPSM , GO to AJ9.
No REPAIR the circuit for high resistance.

Pinpoint Test AL: Voice Recognition Does Not Operate Correctly To Voice Navigate To A Destination

Diagnostic Overview


Refer to Wiring Diagrams Cell 130 for schematic and connector information.

Normal Operation and Fault Conditions

Refer to Information and Entertainment System, Navigation.

Visual Inspection and Diagnostic Pre-checks

  • Verify the key is in the ON position (navigation function may be limited in accessory mode on some vehicles).
  • Verify the vehicle is located in a clear, open area to ensure the satellite information can be received by the vehicle.
  • Verify the navigation Secure Digital (SD) card is present and fully seated in the Secure Digital (SD) card slot.
  • Run the vehicle for at least one minute before testing the system in order for the navigation and voice recognition application to load properly.
PINPOINT TEST AL : VOICE RECOGNITION DOES NOT OPERATE CORRECTLY TO VOICE NAVIGATE TO A DESTINATION
AL1  DETERMINE IF THE VEHICLE IS EQUIPPED WITH A FACTORY-INSTALLED NAVIGATION SYSTEM
  • Make sure the correct VIN was entered on the technician service publication website.
  • Hover the mouse cursor over or click on the OASIS tab toward the top LH corner of the screen.
  • Select HVBoM (Historical Vehicle Bill of Material).
  • Locate the Limit to Base: text entry box toward the center of the screen.
  • Enter the navigation map data Secure Digital (SD) card base part number "19H449" (do not include quotation marks).
  • Press Enter on the keyboard or click on "View BoM (Build of Material)".
    • If the vehicle is equipped with a factory-installed navigation system, a row will appear indicating "CARD-MEMORY" in the DESCRIPTION column.
    • If the vehicle is not equipped with a factory-installed navigation system, a row will not appear and the DESCRIPTION column will be blank.

Does the technician service publication website indicate the vehicle is equipped with a factory-installed navigation system?

Yes GO to AL2.
No Ford Motor Company does not support the addition of a navigation system to vehicles not equipped with a factory-installed navigation system.


AL2  CHECK THE FDIM TOUCHSCREEN RH UPPER TAB
  • Ignition ON.
  • Check the navigation status of the FDIM touchscreen RH upper tab with the vehicle running for at least one minute.

Does the FDIM touchscreen RH upper tab read “NAVIGATION”?

Yes GO to AL4.
No GO to AL3.


AL3  REPROGRAM THE APIM
  • Perform the APIM Standard Programming. Refer to Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) Standard Programming.
  • Override the Service Pack Installation and perform a Full Flash/Force CIP .
  • Once the APIM programming is complete and the system has re-initialized, confirm that the RH upper tab of the FDIM touchscreen displays “NAVIGATION” and the navigation system operates correctly.

Does the RH upper tab of the FDIM touchscreen display “NAVIGATION” and the navigation system operate correctly?

Yes The concern was resolved by reflashing the APIM . TEST the voice recognition system for correct operation.
No GO to AL5.


AL4  VERIFY THAT NO ROUTE PREFERENCE, NAVIGATION, TRAFFIC OR AVOID AREA RESTRICTIONS ARE SELECTED
  • Verify that Route Preferences are not set to avoid freeways, toll roads, ferries and car trains. Refer to the Owner's Literature.
  • Verify that Traffic Preferences are set properly. Refer to the Owner's Literature.
  • Change preferences, as necessary, and operate the Voice Navigation system.

Does the Voice Navigation system operate as expected?

Yes If the concern is not duplicated, the system is operating correctly at this time. ADVISE the customer of the correct operation of the route preference, navigation, traffic and avoid area restrictions.
No GO to AL5.


AL5  CHECK THE AUDIBLE PROMPT FUNCTIONALITY
  • Operate the audio system in AM/FM mode.
  • Operate the VOICE steering wheel switch and listen for the SYNC® audible prompt.

Does the SYNC® system produce an audible prompt correctly indicating voice recognition mode has been entered?

Yes GO to AL6.
No GO to Pinpoint Test N.


AL6  CHECK THE VOICE RECOGNITION OPERATION
  • Operate the VOICE steering wheel switch and listen for the SYNC® audible prompt.
  • NOTE: Make sure the interior of the vehicle is as quiet as possible. Excessive noise may prevent the system from correctly recognizing spoken commands.

    Clearly speak the word "Navigation".

Does the SYNC® system respond correctly to the "Navigation" voice command?

Yes The voice recognition of the navigation system destination concern may have been caused by an insufficiently quiet vehicle or a destination not being present in the map database. GO to AL7.
No GO to Pinpoint Test P.


AL7  CHECK OPERATION OF NAVIGATION SYSTEM WITH MANUAL DESTINATION ENTRY

NOTE: Dragging your finger and pinching two fingers will not scroll to a location or zoom in or out as in other devices on the market. Holding your finger on a location off-center will cause the map to scroll to that location. Refer to the Owner's Literature for more information about navigating the map screen.

  • Using the map feature, touch the screen at the requested destination.
  • Verify there is a road present on the map at the requested location and verify the address of the destination is correct.

Does the navigation system properly navigate to the destination requested?

Yes The information on the navigation secure digital (SD) card may not include the correct map data, or is in a different format than what is expected. The system is operating correctly at this time. NOTIFY the customer that there may be an updated map upgrade available for purchase.
No GO to Pinpoint Test Y.



Pinpoint Test XB: The FDIM Changes Brightness

Diagnostic Overview

Normal Operation and Fault Conditions

The FDIM display brightness can be automatically or manually adjusted. Automatic adjustment relies on the illumination dimming level message sent from the BCM to the APIM .

Possible Sources

  • Customer setting
  • Communication network concern
  • Instrument panel backlighting system concern
  • FDIM
  • APIM
PINPOINT TEST XB : THE FDIM CHANGES BRIGHTNESS
XB1  VERIFY THE DISPLAY BRIGHTNESS CONCERN IS NOT CAUSED BY SYSTEM SETTINGS
  • Using the touchscreen, review the display settings under Settings>Display.
  • Test the system to verify if the concern is caused by a display setting such as Mode being set to "Auto" and Auto Dim turned ON or OFF.

Was the concern caused by a setting within the Display Settings menu?

Yes REVIEW the display brightness settings and system operation with the customer.
No GO to XB2.


XB2  REBOOT THE APIM AND RECHECK THE SYSTEM OPERATION
  • Ignition ON.
  • Simultaneously press and hold the SEEK UP and POWER buttons on the FCIM for 10 seconds. As the APIM reboot begins, the touchscreen turns black before the startup sequence begins.
  • After the reboot is complete, operate the system to verify if the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes GO to XB3.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. VERIFY the customer's specific concern by duplicating the conditions present when the original concern was generated.


XB3  VERIFY OPERATION OF THE NETWORKED INSTRUMENT PANEL BACKLIGHTING SOURCES
  • Illuminate the ambient light sensor to simulate daytime lighting conditions.
  • While adjusting the instrument panel backlighting intensity up and down, inspect the FCIM and IPC .
  • Cover the ambient light sensor to simulate nighttime lighting conditions.
  • While adjusting the instrument panel backlighting intensity up and down, inspect the FCIM and IPC .

Does the instrument panel backlighting operate correctly?

Yes GO to XB4.
No Refer to Section  413-00.


XB4  VERIFY THAT THE APIM AND BCM PASS THE NETWORK TEST
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, perform the network test.

Did the APIM and BCM pass the network test?

Yes GO to XB5.
No Refer to Section  418-00.


XB5  CHECK THE APIM CMDTCS
  • Using a diagnostic scan tool, retrieve all CMDTCs .

Are any CMDTCs present in the APIM ?

Yes REFER to the APIM DTC Chart In this section.
No GO to XB6.


XB6  TEMPORARILY REMOVE THE POWER FROM THE APIM AND RECHECK THE SYSTEM OPERATION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect: Negative Battery Cable from the battery post.
  • Wait for 1 minute.
  • Connect: Negative Battery Cable to the battery post.
  • Ignition ON.
  • Test the system to verify the concern is still present.

Is the concern still present?

Yes GO to XB7.
No The system is operating correctly at this time. VERIFY the customer's specific concern by duplicating the steps that were taken when the original concern was generated.


XB7  CHECK FOR CORRECT APIM OPERATION
  • Ignition OFF.
  • Disconnect and inspect the APIM connector.
  • Repair:
    • Corrosion (clean module pins or install new connectors or terminals)
    • Damaged or bent pins (install new terminals or pins)
    • Pushed-out pins (install new pins as necessary)
  • Reconnect the APIM connector. Make sure it seats and latches correctly.
  • Operate the system and determine if the concern is still present.
